critical.issue: Severity vocabulary mismatch: law_service.SEVERITY_TIERS = {petty, minor, major, capital, regicide} but factions.REPUTATION_CRIME_DELTA = {minor, moderate, major, grievous, regicide}. Calling record_crime(severity='moderate') normalizes severity to 'minor' at law_service.py:191 BEFORE the apply_crime_to_faction hook runs, so reputation moves by -5 instead of the PRD-required -15. Same problem hides 'grievous' (-150) entirely. Only 'minor', 'major', and 'regicide' pass through both vocabularies. PRD's flagship 'moderate=-15' integration is unreachable through the real Law flow.

action_items: [CRITICAL] Align severity taxonomies between law_service.SEVERITY_TIERS and factions.REPUTATION_CRIME_DELTA. rca of the issue: Two independent severity enums were introduced in different modules without a shared source of truth: law_service.py defines {petty, minor, major, capital, regicide} for bounty/sentence purposes; routes/factions.py introduced {minor, moderate, major, grievous, regicide} for reputation delta. The hook at law_service.py:223-228 forwards `severity` to apply_crime_to_faction AFTER line 190-191 silently coerces unknown values to 'minor'. So when the PRD asks for severity='moderate' end-to-end, the hook sees 'minor' and produces -5 instead of -15. Mitigation options: (1) Pick ONE taxonomy across both modules. (2) Add an explicit law-to-rep severity map in factions.apply_crime_to_faction. (3) Drop the silent normalization in law_service and propagate the original severity through to the hook (riskier — breaks bounty math).
